Athleisure
ath-LEE-zher
noun (Millennial slang)
A blend of athletic and leisure, for workout clothing worn as everyday dress: yoga pants and leggings, joggers, hoodies, performance sneakers. The word appears in the late 1970s, but the trend exploded in the 2010s with brands such as Lululemon (founded 1998) and with Millennial wellness culture; Merriam-Webster added athleisure in 2016. By the late 2010s, leggings worn as trousers had become a common flashpoint in debates about modesty and dress codes.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Athleisure is gym clothes worn everywhere: leggings to the grocery store, joggers to class, a hoodie to the office, sneakers with everything. It promises comfort, health, and an always-ready-for-the-gym image. The Christian observation: comfortable clothing is no sin, and exercise is a good stewardship of the body. Paul grants that "bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things" (1Ti 4:8); the body counts for something, though less than the soul. Two things deserve examination. The first is modesty. Some athleisure, especially tight leggings worn as trousers, displays the body in public in a way the same culture would once have reserved for the gym or the home. Scripture asks for "modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety" (1Ti 2:9), and it asks Christians to care whether their dress is a stumbling block to others (Rom 14:13). The second is what the style says: that comfort is the highest value in dress, and that every occasion, including worship, is casual. Clothing communicates; the father of the prodigal put "the best robe" on his son (Luk 15:22) because the occasion was holy and joyful. A father tells his daughter: you are free to be comfortable, and you are called to be modest; do not let the culture decide that leggings are trousers. He tells his son: dress for the occasion, especially on the Lord’s Day, and care about the bodily exercise without making it your religion.

Webster 1828 Definition

Millennial-era fashion term (coined late 1970s; 2010s boom; Merriam-Webster 2016) for workout clothes worn everywhere; comfort and exercise are good, but modesty (1Ti 2:9) and the honour of occasions deserve examination.

ATHLEISURE, n. (Millennial-era fashion term, 2010s; blend of athletic + leisure) Casual clothing designed for exercise and worn as everyday dress: leggings, yoga pants, joggers, hoodies, sneakers.

Webster (1828), root leisure: LEISURE, noun lezh’ur or lee’zhur. 1. Freedom from occupation or business; vacant time; time free from employment. The desire of leisure is much more natural than of business and care. I shall leave with him that rebuke to be considered at his leisure 2. Convenience of time. He sigh’d, and had no leisure more to say. [ Not used .]

Decode for parents: comfort is fine; ask whether the outfit is modest and fits the occasion.

Key Scripture

1Ti 4:8 — "For bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come."

1Ti 2:9 — "In like manner also, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array;"

Rom 14:13 — "Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall in his brother's way."

Luk 15:22 — "But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:"

1Co 6:19 — "What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?"

Modern Corruption

Athleisure makes comfort the highest value in dress and often blurs modesty; Scripture honours the body and exercise but asks for modest, fitting apparel.

expand to see more

The corruption is twofold. First, a casualness that erases occasions: if one outfit fits the gym, the store, school, and church, nothing is set apart, and worship becomes one more errand. Second, a public display of the body that the wearer may not intend but cannot avoid. Tight athletic wear was designed for function in a gym; worn everywhere, it makes the body’s shape the most visible thing about a person. Christian women and men alike should care about that.

The recovery is stewardship without idolatry and comfort without immodesty. "What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you" (1Co 6:19): that verse supports both exercise and modesty. Teach the young to keep their bodies strong, to dress comfortably where comfort fits, to choose modest cuts in public, and to dress up a little for the Lord’s Day, not to impress but to honour.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek athlētēs (contestant) → athletic + Old French leisir (to be permitted) → leisure → late-1970s athleisure → 2010s boom → Merriam-Webster 2016.
